correctness.rationale: For \(f(x)=2x^2\), \(x=1\), and \(\Delta\tau=1/2\), Definition 2.1 gives \(x_{\rm new}=-1\), zero function-value difference, and exactly \(\mathcal K_0=1/(2\sqrt3)\). Assumption 4.1 admits \(\Lambda_1=4\), \(\xi=4\), and every positive Hessian-Lipschitz constant, including \(L=1/100\). The claimed bound is \(5/\sqrt{78}\), strictly larger than the exact step. The repair follows by the correct estimate \(\|G(x_{\rm new})-G(x)\|_2\le B\Delta\tau\|G(x)\|_2\), which contributes \(B^2\) after squaring. The scalar formula \(\mathcal K_0=\sqrt{(z-2)^2+4}/(\lambda\sqrt3)\) proves sharpness of the squared scale.
